ai.title: Brighten CLI input colors and remove dim text
ai.summary: Removed TextAttributes.DIM from multiline-input.tsx, making placeholder text fully visible. Deleted inputBg and inputFocusedBg from theme-system.ts and utils/theme-system.ts, simplifying color logic. Chat.tsx border styling updated to use theme.foreground exclusively, removing secondary border color dependencies.

eli5.text: When you open the app in a terminal and start typing, any helper text that shows up in the input box now appears at full brightness instead of looking faded or gray. Borders and text in the chat window also use a sharper, more consistent color, and the code that picked the input box colors was cleaned up by removing unused options. You wouldn't notice the cleanup itself unless you looked closely, but the main thing you'd see is brighter, easier-to-read typing and borders whenever you use the chat.

ai.title: Dark theme surface and border adjustments in CLI
ai.summary: Dark theme surface shifted to #202327, with muted and border colors brightened to #acb3bf and #536175 respectively. Changes applied to DEFAULT_CHAT_THEMES in cli/src/utils/theme-system.ts.

eli5.text: The dark mode color scheme used in the command-line tool was adjusted for better readability, making background areas a softer dark gray, while text and line colors were slightly brightened for clearer contrast. If you use the command-line version in dark mode, you would notice the interface looks more balanced with less harsh contrast between text and panels. These changes are live today and apply automatically whenever you use the tool with dark theme enabled.

ai.title: Add reasoningdelta event to print mode
ai.summary: New printModeReasoningDeltaSchema added to printModeEventSchema in common/src/types/print-mode.ts. Client.ts updates stream-start logic to trigger on reasoning_delta chunks with empty ancestorRunIds. Scope covers shared core types and CLI client. The event includes text and runId fields, enabling granular reasoning stream handling.

eli5.text: The assistant now sends you smaller, word-by-word updates of its private thinking as it happens, so you can watch the reasoning stream appear live instead of all at once. Only top-level replies get this new streaming behavior today; side-helper reasoning still waits until the end.

ai.title: Version 1.0.511 release bump in npm-app package manifest
ai.summary: The npm-app release package manifest version incremented from 1.0.510 to 1.0.511 in npm-app/release/package.json. This release is grounded in the surrounding same-day commit sequence: Brighten CLI input colors, dark theme surface and border adjustments, add reasoningdelta event to print mode, and route subagent reasoning to agent streams. The release ships notable CLI rendering fixes for suggestion menu arrow keys and multiline input word-wrap cursor navigation, plus a new Button component that resolves a crash on click-and-drag interactions, alongside major agent-runtime changes routing web and docs search through Codebuff web API endpoints with server-reported credit consumption.
ai.evidence: Modified file npm-app/release/package.json shows only a version field change from 1.0.510 to 1.0.511 (+1/-1), a single-line release bump with no other code modifications in the diff.

eli5.text: Version 1.0.511 brings smoother terminal typing, smarter build-mode buttons, a sticky web navbar with blur effects, and new web and docs search endpoints backed by server-side credit billing. The suggestion menu now handles the down-arrow key at the end of a list without glitching. Build-mode buttons stack vertically and use clearer static text. The web navbar stays visible while scrolling and has improved hover animations. You can now use POST endpoints /api/v1/web-search and /api/v1/docs-search with validated input and credit billing. Agent runtime web and docs search now route through Codebuff web API with server-reported credits. Mouse clicks in the CLI no longer crash thanks to a new Button component that prevents text selection. Multiline input cursor navigation is fixed so up/down arrows map to the correct visual lines when text wraps. A paused-message queue shows a border when interrupted and resumes automatically after the next message completes. Input text is brighter and no longer dimmed, improving readability. The dark theme surface and borders have updated colors.

ai.title: Route subagent reasoning to agent streams
ai.summary: SDK `run.ts` converts raw `reasoning` chunks to `reasoning_delta` events carrying `agentId` and `ancestorRunIds`, removing the global `flushReasoning` buffer. CLI `use-send-message.ts` checks `ancestorRunIds.length` to route root reasoning to the main stream and subagent reasoning to `updateAgentContent`, while `npm-app/src/client.ts` drops legacy `reasoning` handling. `common/src/types/print-mode.ts` removes `printModeReasoningSchema`, and `agent-runtime` propagates `ancestorRunIds` through `spawn-agent-utils.ts` and `stream-parser.ts` to track lineage.

eli5.text: When the assistant hires a helper to work on part of your request, that helper's private thinking now shows up in its own section instead of mixing into the main answer. You see helper thoughts grouped under the helper that produced them, while the assistant's own thinking still flows into the main reply. Internally, the system now tags each thought with the helper's identity and family tree, so the screen knows which pane to send it to. Nothing changes about the assistant's own visible response.

ai.title: BYOK OpenRouter support added
ai.summary: Added BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) support for OpenRouter. New constants in `common/src/constants/byok.ts` define `BYOK_OPENROUTER_HEADER` and `BYOK_OPENROUTER_ENV_VAR`. Database migration `0031_damp_hobgoblin.sql` adds a `byok` boolean column to the `message` table. Billing logic in `packages/billing/src/balance-calculator.ts` skips credit consumption when `byok` is true.

eli5.text: You can now tell CodeBuff to use your own OpenRouter API key instead of using theirs. When you run a command, CodeBuff will check for an environment variable named CODEBUFF_BYOK_OPENROUTER and, if it's set, send that key along in a special header so the request is billed to your OpenRouter account. The system was also updated to track these messages and skip charging Codebuff credits when this happens. This is live today for anyone who runs Codebuff with their own OpenRouter key.

ai.title: Add placeholder comment in CLI bootstrap
ai.summary: Added a comment in cli/src/index.tsx within bootstrapCli. No functional changes or logic modifications. Internal codebase adjustment.

eli5.text: A developer added a harmless comment inside the startup code of the program, just a little note that reads "Hi, I created this comment to push a commit to codecane haha." It does not change how the program looks or works; the screen you see and every button behave exactly as before. The only effect is one extra line of text tucked away in the source file, visible only to people reading the code itself.

ai.title: Add base2-with-code-reviewer agent variant
ai.summary: New agent definition `base2-with-code-reviewer` (display name "Buffy the Code Reviewing Orchestrator") added at `.agents/base2/base2-with-code-reviewer.ts`. Extends `createBase2('default', { hasCodeReviewer: true })`. The `hasCodeReviewer` option in `base2.ts` appends `'code-reviewer'` to the sub-agent array and injects a prompt instruction to spawn a code-reviewer agent after edits. Scope: internal agent configs only, no user-facing model picker or CLI changes.

eli5.text: A second automated assistant has been added to the team that checks code changes. It affects the internal agents that review edits, not anything you interact with directly. If you looked, you would see a new agent variant named like a code-reviewing orchestrator and a new option that turns on automatic code review after edits. This is live today in the internal agent configuration only.

ai.title: Add code-reviewer-best-of-n agent suite
ai.summary: New `code-reviewer-best-of-n` orchestrator spawns parallel `code-reviewer-implementor` agents to generate multiple review proposals, then uses a `code-reviewer-selector` to pick the best one. This mechanism replaces single-pass review logic to improve code quality via ensemble selection. The change introduces four new agent definition files in `.agents/reviewer/` and updates `.agents/base2/base2.ts` to register the new orchestrator and its sub-agents. The `createBase2` factory now accepts a `hasCodeReviewerBestOfN` flag to conditionally include the new agent in the spawnable list and prompt instructions.

eli5.text: The assistant can now run several code-review agents at the same time, compare their different suggestions for fixing your code, and then pick the best one to show you instead of just giving the first review it comes up with. This ensemble approach to reviewing code is turned on for the default and GPT-5 versions of the tool, so it's available today whenever those review agents are used. If you look under the hood, you'd see one 'orchestrator' agent spawning a few 'worker' agents to each write a review, followed by a final 'selector' agent that chooses the winner.

ai.title: CLI cancel keeps pending agent response
ai.summary: Cancellation logic now preserves partial assistant output in session state. New getCancelledAdditionalMessages utility wraps pending text in <previous_assistant_message> tags. SDK run.ts replaced early abort checks with deferred state calculation via getCancelledRunState. CLI hook use-send-message.ts updated to store runState before error handling.

eli5.text: When you cancel the assistant mid-response, the CLI now keeps the partial text it had already written instead of throwing it away. That leftover reply is wrapped in a tag so the next turn can pick up where it left off, and the run logic calculates the cancelled session state after storing the previous state. You would notice that cancelling no longer wipes everything the assistant had typed so far. Note: this only affects the CLI flow you actually invoked.

ai.title: Refactor CLI message creation into getUserMessage and getSystemMessage
ai.summary: Added `getUserMessage` and `getSystemMessage` helpers in `cli/src/utils/message-history.ts` to standardize chat message object creation. These functions replace inline object literals in `init.ts`, `router.ts`, `usage.ts`, `use-send-message.ts`, and `slash-commands.ts`, handling ID generation, timestamps, and variant assignment. The refactor supports both string content and `ContentBlock[]` arrays for system and user messages.

eli5.text: When the program needs to show you a message (like a note from the assistant saying it created a file or you typed a question), it now uses a single shared helper to build those messages instead of writing the same setup code over and over in different places. This means the timestamps, IDs and styling of those messages stay consistent everywhere you see them, and any part of the program can hand the helper either plain text or a richer block of content. The change only touches how messages are built behind the scenes, so you won't see a new feature, but chat lines should look uniform and reliable across all the spots the CLI prints them.

ai.title: Block slash commands in CLI router
ai.summary: Added guard in cli/src/commands/router.ts to intercept messages starting with / before agent runtime dispatch. Slash commands now trigger local Command not found system message instead of reaching the agent. Scope limited to CLI router; init command remains exempt. Mechanism prevents unhandled slash syntax from propagating to the agent backend.

eli5.text: When you type a message starting with a slash in the CLI (except the /init command), it now shows a "Command not found" error instead of sending it to the assistant. This means accidental or malformed slash commands won't confuse or interrupt the conversation.

ai.title: GPT-5 code reviewer variants added to base2
ai.summary: Added gpt-5 variants for code reviewer, implementor, and selector agents. `base2.ts` now conditionally selects these gpt-5 specific definitions when `isGpt5` is true. Files moved to `.agents/reviewer/best-of-n/` directory. Removed `reasoning` field from selector output schema.

eli5.text: The code review assistant now has specialized versions built for the latest model, so when that model is in use it picks the right setup instead of the previous one. The review results no longer include a separate explanation field showing how the choice was made. If you use the review feature with the new model, you'll get reviews tailored to that model without the extra reasoning text. This only affects internal reviewers and works automatically once the new model is selected.

ai.title: CLI chat.tsx removes MessageRenderer wrapper, renders
ai.summary: MessageRenderer component removed. Chat.tsx now maps topLevelMessages directly to MessageWithAgents inside scrollbox. message-renderer.tsx renamed to message-with-agents.tsx; MessageRenderer interface and export deleted. Eliminates intermediate component layer.

eli5.text: When you chat with the assistant in the terminal, the program used to wrap each message in an extra helper component before displaying it. The tool now skips that helper and draws each message directly where it belongs on the screen. Nothing about how your messages look or behave changes, you still see the same text and layout, it just uses one fewer layer behind the scenes to put them there.

ai.title: CLI auto-collapse thinking blocks via store
ai.summary: Moved auto-collapse logic from use-send-message.ts to chat-store.ts. Added autoCollapsedAgents state and addAutoCollapsedAgent action. ThinkingBlock now triggers collapse via store updates, removing ref-based tracking. Affects cli/src/chat.tsx, message-block.tsx, message-with-agents.tsx, use-send-message.ts, chat-store.ts.

eli5.text: When the assistant is working through something, you may now see the thinking section automatically fold up so it does not clutter your conversation. Behind the scenes, the rule is now managed in one shared place that every part of the program can check, and it keeps track of which ones should stay folded without you having to do anything. This is already live whenever you see a thinking section appear in the conversation.

ai.title: Fix typecheck in CLI MessageBlock tests
ai.summary: MessageBlock test props updated to match component interface. Added missing autoCollapsedAgents, setCollapsedAgents, and addAutoCollapsedAgent to baseProps in completion and streaming test files. Import order adjusted for lint/typecheck compliance. No runtime behavior change.

eli5.text: The assistant's test files were updated to include the new properties the message-display component now expects, fixing a type-checking error that would have blocked validation. If you looked at the tests, you'd see three new entries added to the sample data: autoCollapsedAgents, setCollapsedAgents, and addAutoCollapsedAgent. This is behind-the-scenes maintenance with no effect on how the assistant appears or behaves.

ai.title: Switch CLI entrypoint to bun shebang
ai.summary: CLI index.tsx now uses #!/usr/bin/env bun shebang. Replaces runtime Bun.main detection and global __CLI_ENTRY_POINT definition with direct bun execution. Imports reordered: polyfills removed, type-only imports moved to end. Covers cli/src/index.tsx.

eli5.text: The command-line tool now starts up using a faster runtime called bun instead of node, so commands you run in your terminal launch a bit differently behind the scenes. You won't see this directly unless you look at how the program is configured to start, but it means the tool is now set up to run with bun from the moment it launches. This only affects people running the assistant from a terminal, and it's already in place today.
